name: State notice filing
what: A state's copy of the Form D notice for a Rule 506 offering, with any fee and consent to service the state requires, usually filed through NASAA's EFD system.

fields.label: State
fields.definition: The state the notice is filed in, and the regulator that receives it, such as the Texas Securities Commissioner. One record per state.

fields.label: Kind of filing
fields.definition: Initial notice, amendment, renewal where the state requires one, or a late initial notice. Read it from the filing confirmation.

fields.label: Form D it copies
fields.definition: The SEC file number and filing date of the Form D or Form D/A the state notice is based on, read from the EDGAR filing.

fields.label: First sale in the state
fields.definition: The date of the first sale to an investor in this state, from the investor register. In Texas it sets the latest date for the notice.

fields.label: Due date
fields.definition: The date the state wants the notice. In Texas it is due when the Form D is filed with the SEC, and no later than 15 days after the first sale in Texas. For any other state, take the date from that state's settings in EFD or its regulator's instructions; leave it empty until read.

fields.label: Date filed
fields.definition: The date the filing system shows the notice as submitted, read from its confirmation.

fields.label: Filed through
fields.definition: NASAA's Electronic Filing Depository (EFD) or the state's own method. Texas requires the Rule 506 notice and fee to go through EFD.

fields.label: Filing confirmation number
fields.definition: The confirmation or filing number the system issued, read from the receipt.

fields.label: Offering amount the fee is based on
fields.definition: The offering amount the notice states and the state fee is computed on. If the issuer later offers more than this, Texas requires an amended Form D and a payment of three times the fee shortfall plus interest, unless the maximum fee was paid.

fields.label: State fee paid
fields.definition: The state's filing fee as charged on the receipt. Texas sets its fee by statute, which its rule cites.

fields.label: EFD system fee paid
fields.definition: The filing system's own fee, as charged on the receipt, recorded apart from the state fee.

fields.label: Payment method and approver
fields.definition: How the fees were paid, such as ACH through EFD, and the person who approved the payment. Never the bank account details.

fields.label: Consent to service of process
fields.definition: Whether this state requires a separate consent to service of process with the notice and, if so, whether one is on file and where. Texas's rule for a Rule 506 notice asks for the Form D and the fee.

fields.label: How long the notice stays effective
fields.definition: The period the state gives the notice. In Texas a Rule 506 notice stays effective until the offering is completed or terminated, so there is no annual renewal. For another state, read the period in EFD or its rules.

fields.label: Renewal due
fields.definition: The next renewal date where the state requires one. Empty for Texas Rule 506 notices and for any state not yet researched.

fields.label: Where the receipt is kept
fields.definition: Where the firm keeps the filed notice, the fee receipt and any consent to service.
